text:
Arseny Gritsyuk was a fifth-round pick in 2019 who spent years in the KHL before the Devils brought him over, and in his second NHL season he has become a real piece. Nineteen points in 26 games at 15:35 a night, five on the power play, and the shootout winner against Columbus on Nov. 25.

The goal total is the part to treat carefully. Eight goals on 6.1 expected, and none in his last ten games, which tells you the early stretch ran hot and has since cooled. The assists kept coming: seven in that same ten-game span. His 2.81 points per 60 minutes is above the top of our talent range, so some regression in the overall pace is likely even if the play holds.

The play does hold. New Jersey controls 59% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, nearly four points better than without him, and his linemates are finishing right at their chances. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking said 53% of his shots came off the rush last season. Watch the shots: 59 in 26 games, enough that the goals should come back.
